companyRankingLists.itemDescription:
One by one, over the past year, many major retailers caved under pressure from conservative groups to weaken their diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) programs. But one chain bucked that trend: Costco Wholesale.

In December, conservative think tank National Center for Public Policy Research submitted a shareholder proposal that would have required Costco to evaluate DEI initiatives which it claimed hold “litigation, reputational and financial risks.” Hogwash, Costco’s board responded: DEI is good business, its directors said.

“As our membership diversifies, we believe that serving it with a diverse group of employees enhances satisfaction,” Costco wrote. Costco shareholders and customers seem to agree. In the shareholder proxy vote, 98% of votes cast opposed the proposal. In the first three quarters of this fiscal year, net sales were up 8%, outperforming most competitors; and surveys of customer satisfaction suggested that no Costco users were defecting.

image.title: G500 2022-26-Costco Wholesale
image.caption: ORLANDO, FLORIDA, UNITED STATES - 2022/05/31: Shoppers wait in a check-out line at a Costco wholesale store in Orlando. Costco reported a double-digit rise in sales during the third quarter and record numbers of new members as consumers look for ways to fight rising food prices caused by inflation.
image.credit: Paul HennessySOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images

companyRankingLists.itemDescription: Costco had a smashing 2021, closing the year in record-breaking style as the pandemic eased and shoppers returned to in-person shopping at their favorite retailers. Costco's $5 billion in net income was 25% higher than in the year prior. With inflation surging to a four-decade high, the wholesaler raised its prices but still saw a 91% membership renewal rate. Like many other employers in the U.S., Costco raised its minimum wage in the fight to retain talent, upping that rate to $17 in October 2021. The warehouse supermarket giant partnered with Uber to trial a delivery service in Texas, and it collaborated with public health authorities to help get America vaccinated against COVID. Seeing more foot traffic in its stores, Costco debuted touchless condiment dispensers in its food courts, and brought back customer favorites like churros and smoothies to its menu. Costco pleased investors as well as shoppers in 2021 by delivering a 52% shareholder return for the year.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription: Despite the pandemic, Costco Wholesale drew throngs of shoppers to its stores, as consumers looked to buy everyday staples in bulk. The company quickly adapted to the crisis conditions, making mask-wearing mandatory and giving workers permanent raises to keep them motivated, moves that fueled a 9.2% increase in sales last fiscal year. In addition, Costco’s e-commerce apparatus finally went into high gear, allowing it to better compete against Sam’s Club, among others. Costco’s momentum has continued into 2021, with its hold on members as strong as ever.

companyRankingLists.title: Change the World
companyRankingLists.itemDescription: In the war for retail talent during the pandemic, Costco Wholesale put its money where its mouth is. Already a leader in incentives like paid sick days, Costco in February raised the internal minimum wage for its 200,000-plus–person workforce to $16, keeping the pressure on competitors to pay their own workers more. Not long afterward, Amazon and Walmart each gave raises to hundreds of thousands of their workers. Costco’s reward for its efforts: double-digit percentage increases in sales—long after pandemic panic-buying eased—and customers as loyal as ever.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription: With 782 stores and 99 million membership-card holders worldwide, Costco had a strong 2019, posting an 8% increase in overall revenue. That reflected a 6% boost in same store sales and a 7% gain in membership revenue. Profits, meanwhile, jumped 17%. The company opened its first store in China, located in western Shanghai, last year, and had 139,000 membership sign-ups on its first day of operation there. The retailer has been pushing to expand its ecommerce offerings, including click-and-collect, as well as offering same-day grocery delivery in most of its U.S. locations. It has also begun looking at vertical integration, investing in its own poultry processing plant in Nebraska and in a California greenhouse growing organic lettuce to supply its stores.

companyRankingLists.description: Global business is back. After limping through a worldwide financial crisis and economic slowdown, the 500 largest companies ranked by revenues shattered all sorts of performance records in 2013: They racked up combined revenues of $31.1 trillion, up 2.5% from 2012, and profits soared 27% to nearly $2 trillion. China’s 95 companies (up from 89 last year) posted $5.8 trillion in revenues. The U.S. has four fewer companies on the list than last year but remains (for now) the country leader, with 128 corporations on the list—including No. 1 Wal-Mart Stores—reporting $8.6 trillion in revenues.
